compared: resolver cases: the ids every round the model asks ends with; the reuse case: the final text, the number of sends, every message of the last request (role, call ids, result id, text) and the distinct ids onToolResult saw, in order (Node calls it twice per result; the Rust replay reads the results from the transcript)

excluded.src/runtime/agent/orchestrator/session/t: difference: Node resolves a batch it did not see streamed as a whole, keeping the unclaimed a-2 and moving the clash past it ([a-3, a-2]); Rust resolves every call as it streams, which gives [a-2, a-2-2] (what Node's streamed path gives for the same calls)
not representable: a Rust stream call always carries an id (the codec gives one to a call the provider sent without), so the id-less call has no replay
